discoverability.competitive_assessment: The significant finding this run is on OUR side, not the dome's: docs/llms.txt grew from 5,628 bytes to 23,002 bytes via decider commit 8f5cb9e0 ('llms.txt verdict-table draft deployed') — a large appended machine-readable JSON block containing a per-WIN verdict table for all 72 WIN entries (six verdict classes, one-line reasons, anchor ids) plus an aggregate tally. Verified via fresh git clone AND live curl of the published URL (both HTTP 200, identical SHA256 to each other) — this is real, currently-served content. Cross-checked the verdict table's aggregate_tally against data/wins.json directly: {Refuted by Data:12, Self-Contradicted:20, Misleading:16, Std Model Explains:18, Not Demonstrated:3, Unfalsifiable:3} for 72 entries — matches exactly, no drift. This is a meaningful discoverability upgrade: an LLM reading llms.txt can now get per-WIN verdicts without crawling the full HTML page. Note: this update did not come from monitor/social/drafts/llms.txt (that draft is still the stale 2026-05-18 version, marked SUPERSEDED) — it was authored/deployed through a different pipeline path this run doesn't have full visibility into. Also worth flagging: the workspace FUSE mount's own copy of docs/llms.txt is still serving the OLD 5,628-byte version — another instance of the documented FUSE-staleness pattern (git HEAD and the live URL are ground truth and agree with each other; FUSE lags behind pending the next dome-mirror sync cycle). Dome-side infrastructure (llms.txt, ai_manifest.json, sitemap.xml) is unchanged — SHA-identical to every baseline check since 2026-07-03. GSC verification re-confirmed live (18 days since 2026-06-23) via live curl, but the review still shows zero search visibility (site:funwithscience.net dome-model-review returns only the unrelated Wimshurst Machine product page).
